Turkish football giants Galatasaray have apologised to supporters following the relocation of their home match against Samsunspor to Başakşehir Fatih Terim Stadium due to ongoing pitch renovation work. The club announced that the fixture would no longer take place at their home stadium, explaining that the renovation was necessary to provide the team with the best possible playing conditions. In a statement to supporters on Wednesday on its X handle, Galatasaray acknowledged the inconvenience and disappointment caused by the decision, particularly among season ticket holders. The club said, “We regret that we will not be able to welcome our team and supporters to our home ground for this match. “We are aware of the inconvenience and disappointment this decision has caused all our supporters, particularly our season ticket holders.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. The priority ticket sales window will run from 11am on Thursday, November 19, until 3pm on Friday, November 20. The club also announced that an amount equivalent to the ticket price paid for their most recent home match would be deducted from the cost of renewing or purchasing season tickets for the following season. Galatasaray said the measures were introduced in recognition of the loyalty and sacrifices of supporters who continue to back the club. The Turkish champions also reaffirmed their determination to pursue a fifth consecutive league title under their #Hedef27 campaign, promising to continue their efforts with the support of their fans. The statement added, “We know that what makes Galatasaray feel at home is not just its stadium, but its great supporters, who are always by its side.” The club expressed appreciation for the understanding of supporters and reiterated that their backing remained crucial as the team continued its pursuit of domestic success.
